solution: f is an iterated morphism (a D0L system): every letter c is rewritten as the fixed word T_c, and since every |T_c| >= 2 the expansion of a single letter after k rounds has length at least 2^k. Because every queried position is at most 10^15 < 2^50, at any level deeper than 50 the position is forced to lie inside the expansion of the FIRST character, so the top K-50 steps of the descent are the deterministic map g(c) = first letter of T_c, a functional graph on 26 nodes; folding it by rho/cycle detection (tail plus cycle is at most 26) yields g^(K-50)(S[0]) in O(26) time, which replaces S by that one letter and K by 50. With K' = min(K,50) the lengths L[k][c] = |f^k(c)| are then built bottom-up with saturating addition capped just above 10^15 (so the true value is recovered exactly whenever it is below the cap, which is all the descent ever compares against), one prefix pass over S decides which letter of S owns each query, and each query walks down at most 50 levels, scanning the at most 50 children per level to find the one containing the remaining offset. The whole answer for a query is thus read off without ever materialising the string, and the per-query work is bounded because the fold above level 50 is forced rather than chosen. Time is O(|S| + 26*K'*maxT + M*K'*maxT), about 3 million operations at |S| = 10^6, K = 10^15, M = 1000, and space is O(|S| + 26*K') for the prefix sums and the small length table.

solution_source.used: Reconstructed the two ideas the slides name (cut K down to 50 by the cycle in the first-character map; recurse level by level using expansion lengths), transcribed them into verify_prolongedpassword.py, confirmed both statement samples, and cross-checked against a literal expansion of f^K(S) on 400 random morphisms with the query bound shrunk so full expansion is feasible -- 342 of those trials actually exercised the fold, all matched.

statement_summary: A password starts as a lowercase string of up to a million letters and is grown by simultaneously replacing every letter with a fixed word assigned to that letter, each word at least two letters long, repeating that substitution as many as a quadrillion times. For up to a thousand forgotten positions, none beyond a quadrillion, the task is to report which letter stands at each of those positions.
notes: The debrief is one PDF covering two problems; the extraction is rough (10^15 renders as '1015', and the 26x26 matrix loses its layout -- its printed bottom row repeats N_aa..N_zz where it must be N_za..N_zz), but the two slides that carry the algorithm survive intact and the cycle example on them is decisive: 'a -> bda, b -> cdc, c -> ab' is annotated 'abca', which is exactly the orbit of the FIRST-character map g(a)=b, g(b)=c, g(c)=a. That pinned down the fold and it then reproduced both samples and every randomized cross-check. matrix-exponentiation is deliberately at 0.35: the judges compute the length vector as r*N^K by binary matrix power and the slide summary says 'solve by recursing and using matrix exponentiation', so the label is faithful to the published route, but it is NOT load-bearing -- their own previous slide caps K at 50 to stop the lengths overflowing, and after that cap 50 saturating matrix-vector products (or just a 26x51 DP table, which is what the verify script does) give the same lengths, so no exponentiation is needed and no searcher should expect this to be a matrix-power problem. Deliberately omitted: binary-search and prefix-sum (locating which letter of S owns a query is real work, since a per-query rescan of S would be 10^9 at |S| = 10^6 and M = 1000, but a prefix pass plus binary search is generic scaffolding), and offline-queries (the debrief's fix is to sort the queries and answer them in one pass over S, which is only one of two ways to avoid that 10^9 -- prefix sums need no offline step, so the label would overstate it). Vocabulary gap: the corpus has no term for the actual shape of this problem -- indexing into an iterated morphism / D0L system, i.e. descending a self-similar expansion by subtree sizes to reach the n-th leaf; something like iterated-substitution or kth-element-descent would be the precise label, and the saturating-arithmetic trick that keeps the lengths finite has no name either. Nothing in the source text was addressed to a reader or an agent.
